comments.note: graph.py module docstring (line 7) still reads 'Six pipeline-stage nodes from src.nodes' and the ASCII topology diagram only shows pm, developer, qa, reviewer, docs, synthesis — omitting security_auditor and release_engineer. The functional implementation is correct; only the documentation is stale. Suggest updating to 'Eight pipeline-stage nodes' and adding the two new lines to the topology diagram in a follow-up.

test_supervisor_node_present and test_synthesis_node_present in test_graph.py are now fully subsumed by test_graph_has_nine_nodes which asserts equality of the complete node set. The two spot-check tests are harmless but redundant. Can be removed in a future cleanup.

config.py PIPELINE_PREREQUISITES treats all 6 stages as a mandatory linear chain (security-audit prerequisite is qa, code-review prerequisite is security-audit, etc). This hardcodes the 9-agent full-pipeline assumption into the orchestrator — WPs using active_pipeline_stages to skip security-audit or release-engineering would be mis-routed. This is acknowledged known simplification from WP-007 scope (the orchestrator is simpler than the MCP server's composition engine). Recommend documenting this limitation in orchestrator/README.md or ARCHITECTURE.md as a known constraint.

Gold Nugget: the GUI inactive-stage rendering pattern — build a presentSet and activeSet from the WP data, then iterate PIPELINE_STAGES to generate badges with a three-way signal (present/missing/inactive) — is clean and extensible. Same pattern should be applied to any future status dashboards in the GUI.
